route-a: Route A, the front door, quiet (GDD v0.26.0 §07; Keel N11), fight it out (brief 018 §5). The Scout watches Inez and listens; the Tech loops the entrance camera at 1:25 (live 1:45 to 3:45, so it still runs at the Enter) and takes no Reroute (brief 067 A: the patrol sweeps the service yard, not the door; informed play doesn't pay 1 T for nothing); the Fixer helps Inez twice (the cast's Inez is Fearful, §04) and has her call the guard away; the Enforcer enters while the door is unwatched and comes out by the service door with Vale. He holds Vale at (20.0, -65.0), 20.4 m from the car and 20.8 m or more from every ambush spot (Motive's ra-h3, briefs/067/motive.md §1.5), beyond the pistol's 16 m, so the cell's fire springs the ambush; the three fight the rival crew until it breaks (fight.over), then he boards with Vale and the car leaves at once; the three, on a calm street, walk out at no cost. c038 (Waymark, engine 0.34.1): the cell walks at 1.8 m/s and its runs are noticed, never an Alert, so route A ends at Alert 0.
route-a-board: Route A, board and go (brief 018 §5), the route's primary: the same route as route-a to the ambush (no Reroute: the patrol sweeps the service yard, brief 067 A); then the Enforcer walks Vale to the car as it springs, the three fire until the blocker is down, then board, and the car leaves with the whole cell. Route A, the front door, quiet (GDD v0.26.0 §07; Keel N11): watch and listen to Inez, loop the entrance camera at 1:25, help Inez as often as the card asks (twice: the cast's Inez is Fearful, §04) and have her call the guard away, enter while the door is unwatched, take Vale out by the service door, and fight the rivals' ambush at the getaway car with the whole armed cell (Arms 3). The cell runs where a player in a hurry would (to the café, the cabinet and the door): a run is noticed, never an Alert (engine 0.34.0), so the quiet route ends at Alert 0.
route-a-pressure: Route A with Pressure for Help (Keel S25; Sky Q4), fight it out: Pressure leans on Inez's affair, learned by Listen ($0, +3 T); the cast's Inez is Fearful, so it is also her own approach and one order turns her, and she calls the guard away at about 1:46. No Reroute (brief 067 A). c038 (Waymark, engine 0.34.1): the Enforcer goes to the door from 2:40, not as soon as she calls: Pressure brings no warning from Inez, and Vale out before the rival car posts (2:24 on the call's timing) meant all five coming hot at the Enforcer with no posts (the c037 script lost rivals-reach-vale at 3:17.2; composed fresh it won 3 of 8 jitters). Out at about 3:20, after the crew has posted, he holds Vale at (20.0, -65.0) as route-a does while the three break the crew, then boards; the car leaves at once and the three walk out. Faster than route-a by the Pressure's one turn, at 2 T more and no money.
route-a-pressure-board: Board and go (brief 018 §5), the twin of route-a-pressure: the same route to the ambush (Pressure for Help, no Reroute, the Enforcer at the door from 2:40 so Vale comes out to the posted crew, c038); then the Enforcer holds Vale 19.5 m out while the three fire, walks him in once the blocker is out (Motive briefs/067/motive-square.md §7), boards, the three board after him, and the car leaves with the whole cell. Pressure brings no warning from Inez, so the five fire at once.
route-a-disable: Route A (fight it out) with Disable in place of the Loop (brief 058 §4, §6): the cut (+2 T, where the loop is +1) is reported by the desk at its next scan, the run's first incident (Alert 1); route A has no later report, so it wins at the same time as route-a and one Trail dearer, with no 2:00 window to keep. No Reroute (brief 067 A): the patrol answers the dead screen and stands down without a report. The Enforcer holds Vale at (20.0, -65.0) as route-a does (Motive's rad-h3).
route-b: Route B, the pickup, quiet (GDD v0.26.0 §07; Keel N11b), fight it out (brief 018 §5). The Scout listens to the driver and the Fixer pays him by 5:40 ($70,000); his word sends the rivals' lookout off; the Scout gives the rival car a false tip at 3:10; the Tech reroutes the patrol from the cabinet at 5:00 (it lands at 5:45 and keeps the yard clear to 7:40: brief 067 A, the patrol sweeps the service yard; rerouted it never breaks to the yard fight), then runs to the getaway car and Drives it round behind Vale's car once it parks in the service bay (car.parks). The Enforcer waits at the square until 5:50 (in the yard before the Reroute the patrol reported him at 1:53.4), walks to the service lane, takes Vale from the back seat (38 s, off-screen) and carries him 3.5 m to the car. The posted three run after the Driven car and spring at the Take; the Fixer and then the Scout, 0.5 s later (Motive's rb-st: on the same tick the Fixer took both rivals' fire and went down), lock rival-1 then rival-2 (focus fire, Motive M059-B7: at will the three shoot the carrying Enforcer down) until the crew breaks; then Go. The three left behind on a calm street walk out.
route-b-board: Route B, board and go (brief 018 §5), the route's primary: as route-b to the Take (the driver paid, the false tip, the Reroute at 5:00, the car Driven round behind Vale's, the Enforcer at the square until 5:50); then the Enforcer carries Vale 3.5 m into the car while the Fixer and the Scout (0.5 s after him) lock rival-1 then rival-2, and once the blocker is down the two board and the car leaves with the whole cell.
route-b-thin: Route B thinned (brief 059 S1; Motive's s1-rulings route-b-thin): route-b with one posted rival taken down before the pickup where the other two cannot see it. At 5:28 the Enforcer, waiting at the square, knocks out rival-3 at his lone post by the café terrace from behind (1.3 m off his back; he faces our car), 28 m from the pair on the square's east side, beyond their pistols' 16 m, and leaves him; he wakes after the fight. At the Take the floor (rivals-floor 3) recalls the warned lookout and the tipped car, so the fight is the two posted plus the late two: thinner, never skipped (MC-14). The knockout costs nothing while nobody reports it before the car leaves (a passer-by finds him at 7:30 and is still walking over).
route-g: Route G, knockout (brief 013 D; Motive 013 §6.1 G-KO), fight it out: the Scout watches the guard (his cone and check-in marks), the Tech loops the entrance camera at 1:00, and the Enforcer knocks the guard out from beside just after his 2:30 mark and leaves him where he fell, enters at once and takes Vale out by the service door. No Reroute (brief 067 A: the patrol sweeps the service yard, and nothing is carried into it). He holds Vale at (24.0, -60.0) while the Scout, Fixer and Tech lock rival-2 then rival-1 (focus fire, Motive M059-B7) until the crew breaks; then he boards and the car leaves; the three walk out.
route-g-board: Board and go (brief 018 §5), the twin of route-g: the same route to the ambush (no Reroute); then the Enforcer walks Vale to the car as it springs while the three lock rival-2 then rival-1, and once the blocker is down they board and the car leaves with the whole cell.
route-g-fast: Route G, fast (brief 013 D; Motive 013 §6.1 G-fast), fight it out: route G with the loop as soon as the Tech reaches the cabinet (live 0:32.7 to 2:32.7) and the guard knocked out at about 1:26, from beside, as the Enforcer walks in at 1:17 (when the patrol left the door, before brief 067 A moved it to the yard: no Reroute now). He enters at once (out at about 2:11), holds Vale at (24.0, -60.0) while the three lock rival-1, rival-2 and rival-3 in turn from the spring (focus fire, Motive M059-B7), and boards once the crew breaks; the three walk out. The fastest quiet win (MC-6).
route-g-fast-board: Route G, fast, board and go (brief 018 §5), the route's primary: as route-g-fast to the ambush (the loop at once, the guard knocked out at about 1:26 with no Reroute, the Enter at once); then the Enforcer walks Vale to the car as it springs while the three lock rival-1, rival-2 and rival-3 in turn, and once the blocker is down they board and the car leaves with the whole cell.
route-g-kill: Route G with a kill (brief 013 D; Motive 013 §6.1 G-kill), fight it out: the guard killed (3 s) and his body carried to the Office's service door and put through it, never found in the mission (a missing person, an open case: GDD §07 kill variant). The Tech reroutes the patrol before the carry (brief 067 A: the yard's sweep would see the carry; Motive briefs/067/motive-square.md §5.2). The Enforcer holds Vale at (20.0, -65.0) while the three fight the crew until it breaks (SQ2: a rival with nobody in reach advances on the op, so the fight ends), then boards; the three walk out.
route-g-kill-board: Board and go (brief 018 §5), the twin of route-g-kill: the same route to the ambush (the kill, the carry through the service door with the patrol rerouted); then the Enforcer holds Vale at (20.0, -65.0) until the blocker is out and only then walks him in (Motive's rgkb-bo: walking in at the spring crossed the blocker's lane walk, and the blocker fires as he walks), boards, the three board after him, and the car leaves with the whole cell.
loud: The loud reference, board and go (GDD v0.26.0 §07 loud; Keel N10; brief 018 §5): loop the camera and reroute the patrol, shoot the guard just after his 2:30 mark (gunfire: Alert 2, the shots traced), enter (68 s at Alert 2), and take Vale out by the service door. The gunfire draws the rival car to the Office front (16 s), four of them on foot; when the final fight opens (police from the north street, the seal clock running) the Scout, Fixer and Tech down the response unit (security-2 then security-1, the blocker), then the Scout and Fixer flank across the square and drop rival-1, rival-2 and rival-3 in turn (traced: they are not the final fight's hostiles), until the crew breaks (§06: more than half down; Motive M059-B5, S11's shape: break the drawn crew before Vale is walked into it). Only then does the Enforcer walk Vale to the car; the three board after him and the car leaves with officers 1 and 2 still at their stands: one of them sees it go (+1 T, the car hunted).
loud-fight: Fight it out, the loud twin (brief 018 §5): as loud to the Enforcer's Board; then he steps out again (Vale stays in) and the whole cell, his carbine with the three sidearms, downs the final fight's two officers on the café wall (the police never break; three sidearms alone lose to two trained officers on this engine), and only then do they board: the seal clock runs, so anyone left standing would be captured. Nobody is up to see the car go, so it costs 1 T less than loud.
loud-left-downed: Brief 018 §5: the run that leaves a downed op. Loud (board and go) with the Scout sent out of cover toward the officers on the café wall when the rivals break: she is downed, nobody carries her, and the car leaves without her, so she is captured (downed) and +4 T goes to the campaign.
loud-left-standing: Brief 018 §5: the run that leaves a standing op mid-fight. Loud (board and go) without the Scout boarding: the blocker is down and the car free, but the officers at their stands are still up, so the Scout, left standing, is captured (fighting: abandoned, resentment +1, loyalty -1) and +4 T goes to the campaign.
fight-safe-cell-down: §07 fail 'the cell down (every op down)' (GDD v0.26.0; Motive M067-K3 b; Keel K3-CELL-DOWN), in the safe fight: route-g-fast-board to the spring (no contact touched), but the cell will not fight at the car: the three draw (a cause for the rivals, §06) and hold their fire, and the Enforcer walks Vale in, boards him and steps out again to stand by the car, drawn, holding fire. Someone of the cell always stands outside, so the rivals keep their cover (no walk to the held car, K3 a); with nobody in reach they advance on the four (SQ2) and shoot them down one by one, and the mission fails the tick the last falls.
fight-loud-wait-square: MC-13 (brief 059, Motive M059-5.3), the square's loud-wait twin: loud's opening (the guard shot just after his 2:30 mark, the Enter at Alert 2), but the cell waits in the car: the Scout, Fixer and Tech board while the Enforcer is inside, and nobody fights the response unit or the rivals drawn by the gunfire. He walks Vale out toward the car alone and is shot down on the way (Enforcer down before Vale is in the car): the square opens no unfought loud exit.
fight-loud-wait-yard: MC-13 (brief 059, Motive M059-5.3; Keel's P59-LOUD-YARD), the service drive's loud-wait twin: route-b-board to the pickup, but the Fixer shoots the pickup camera out as Vale's car parks (gunfire: Alert 2), and the Scout and Fixer get into the car the Tech drove round. The Enforcer takes Vale from the back seat, carries him 3.5 m and boards, and Go is refused: the car is held (the official entrance's officers, the nearest entry to the stand, §07 loud: their blocker on the lane). Nobody of the cell fights, so the car can't leave, and the player withdraws (the free abort). Left to wait, the run seals (9:47.7 under the rulebook's final intent, agent) or, under the control intent every, the police shoot the cell down in the car: the Withdraw keeps the twin to what MC-13 reads, the refusal.
careless-reporter-not-stopped: Careless violence (brief 013 D), the twin of route-b: the idle Enforcer kills guard 73 (p-records-office-73, the incoming door guard) on his walk from the café to the public door and leaves him where he fell. c038 (Waymark, engine 0.34.1): his walk now runs 3.5 m south of the old spot (walks off the grid since 0.33.0), so the Enforcer waits 1.2 m beside the new line at (33.0, -40.1); the kill (about 4:30) is timed to his arrival, the first tick he is in reach, from the side, unseen. His missed 5:30 mark is the desk's report (Alert 1), which no Tech action stops; nobody finds the body before the car leaves, so the debrief carries a missing person and an open case: a win at Alert 1 (route-b: Alert 0) and dearer in total Trail (MC-7).
careless-scout-idles-pickup: Careless loiter (brief 031), the twin of route-b: route-b, but the Scout waits for the 3:10 tip in the pickup camera's view: reported as a loiterer at its desk's next scan (Alert 1, the dial's two robots, no Trail); the route still wins, one Alert dearer than its twin (Alert 0). As route-b: the Reroute at 5:00, the Enforcer at the square until 5:50, the Scout's lock 0.5 s after the Fixer's.
careless-g-disable: Careless (brief 058 §4, §6), the twin of route-g: route G with Disable in place of the Loop (at 1:10): the desk's report of the dead screen is the first incident (Alert 1), and the knocked-out guard, found at the door while the cell is still at the car, is the second (Alert 2, before the fight is over). The Tech reroutes the patrol at 1:46 as c037's twin did: without it the patrol answers the dead screen at the camera and the run goes loud and seals (probed on 0.34.1). Focus fire as route-g (Motive M059-B7): the three lock rival-2 then rival-1 from the spring.
careless-thin-all: Careless violence (brief 059 S1; Motive's s1-rulings careless-thin-all), the twin of route-b: the Enforcer sets out to take down all three posted rivals on the square before the pickup. The lone one by the café terrace goes down unseen (as route-b-thin), but the pair on its east side cannot be thinned quietly (M059-S1.6): rival-2 sees rival-1 taken down and draws, the Enforcer shoots him, and the run is loud from then on (the shots traced, Alert 2 when the bodies are found), so the yard fight is the police from the official entrance; the car goes once their blocker is down, leaving the Scout and Fixer behind.
careless-loop-runs-out: Careless timing (brief 058 §6; Loop v2: a loop runs 2:00 from its landing), the twin of route-a: route-a with the loop planted first, as soon as the Tech reaches the cabinet (live 0:32.7 to 2:32.7), not at 1:25: it has run out 20 s before the Enter at about 2:53, and the entrance camera sees it (entry seen by a live camera).
careless-enforcer-watches-guard: Careless (brief 031 §7; Sky 2026-10-20 D1: being seen watching makes the target wary), the twin of route-g-fast: route-g-fast, but the Enforcer lingers beside the guard (1.2 m, inside his 3 m sense) for about 25 s before the knockout, where route-g-fast strikes as he arrives: the guard's attention clock runs to wary (Heat 0: 20 s), a wary guard is aware at the blow, he draws, the takedown fails, and the Enforcer goes down. c038: route-g-fast takes no Reroute, so neither does its twin; the Enforcer's own Watch is refused once the Scout has watched the guard, so he simply stands there.
